figures.caption: Figure 1: Example 1 as a sequence of MDP transitions. The agent is on roll and owns the cube (state s), shown with its cube-ownership one-hot vector c and is_cube_action flag. no_double transitions directly to the agent’s checker play (sno-recube); offer_double hands the opponent a take/drop decision, which the on-roll agent computes analytically (drop iff 2V (srecube) > 1). A take leads to srecube (the opponent now owns the cube); a drop ends the game with the agent winning the current cube value. Solid arrows are state transitions; dashed arrows mark the TD update that backs the realized next-state value up to V (s).

Figure 2: Strength of prob5 during training. Head-to-head equity against gnubg at 0-ply is measured at ten checkpoints of the run in Table 13, with 95% confidence intervals (the first five checkpoints use 106 evaluation games and the rest 2 × 106). The horizontal axis counts all self-play episodes behind each checkpoint, including the ≈42M episodes of the shared base inherited from step 17 of Table 12. The single largest gain comes from stage 2, the first 1M episodes of 1-ply training, which is worth about +12 mEq/game. The dashed line and gray band mark the production prob5 model’s 46.3 [45.5, 47.2] mEq/game against the same opponent (Table 2).

Figure 3: Strength of the cubeful retraining run. Head-to-head equity against the production cubeful model is measured over the course of the run in Table 14, with 95% confidence intervals; zero marks parity with the production model. As in Figure 2, the horizontal axis counts all self-play episodes behind each checkpoint, here including the ≈55M episodes of the DMP and cubeless-equity stages that precede the first cubeful episode.
